sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed: BRIL N-terminal fusion rescued low surface expression of wild-type hGPRC5D (PMC11187071). GPCR signaling function NOT MEASURED in the cited study.
sites.rationale: The topology assigns residues 1–23 as extracellular with no signal peptide (raw topology begins 'O'), making residue 1 (M) the mature N-terminus and insert_after_residue=0 the only unambiguous extracellular N-terminal junction. The paper names 'N-terminus' without a residue number, so position_evidence is topology_derived. L2 (same paper) independently confirms that the N-terminal BRIL fusion restored surface expression, satisfying the surface_only validation threshold. The 23-residue extracellular span before TM1 (residues 1–23) provides ample clearance (≥3 residues) from the TM boundary for a short epitope tag. Full-length membrane-anchored hGPRC5D expressed in HEK293 cells with an HA signal peptide, Flag tag, and thermostabilized BRIL domain fused to the N-terminus; the fusion overcame low surface expression of wild-type receptor and enabled cryo-EM structural and ligand-binding studies.

sources.claim: Haemagglutinin signal peptide, Flag tag, and thermostabilized Escherichia coli apocytochrome b562RIL (BRIL) 41 , 42 were added on the N-terminus to increase the expression yield of GPRC5D.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are provided (L1, L2), both from PMC11187071, both describing the same N-terminal Flag+BRIL fusion construct on full-length membrane-anchored GPRC5D. No ledger evidence supports insertions in ECL1 (83–93), ECL2 (150–169), or ECL3 (226–241), so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminus (residues 263–345) is intracellular per the topology landmarks and is therefore excluded from surface tag sites. The BRIL domain is much larger than a short epitope tag (~13–23 aa), but the ledger line establishes that the N-terminal extracellular face tolerates a large fusion, making it a fortiori suitable for a short ALFA-type tag. No signal peptide is present in the canonical sequence topology, so no upstream cleavage concern applies.
